messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: dsm 2.0 released, now on CRAN
parts:
Dear all,

The R library dsm is now available on CRAN as part of it's 2.0 release.
The package implements spatial modelling for distance sampling data as
in Hedley and Buckland ("Spatial Models for Line Transect Sampling",
JABES 2004).

I advise all users of dsm in R (_not_ Distance for Windows) to upgrade.

Version 2.0 fixes a series of bugs, now includes better documentation
and examples. The syntax has been greatly simplified from previous
versions and now operates similarly to the popular mgcv package.

Features include:
* fitting of models with counts, estimated abundance, density
* use a detection function fitted with Distance or mrds pacakges
* standard GAM diagnostics
* uncertainty estimation using GAM theory or moving block bootstrap
* easy plotting of both smooths and uncertainty maps
* use of any smooth basis available to mgcv, including the soap film
smoother for complex regions (peninsulae, islands etc) (and if you're
adventurous you can write you're own)
* for more information about new features see
http://dill.github.com/posters/dsm-poster-isec2012.pdf
* for a worked example using marine mammal data, see
https://github.com/dill/dsm/wiki/mexico-analysis

Please do make sure that you have updated to the newest versions of R,
mgcv, Distance and mrds (update.packages() in R) before attempting to
use dsm.

Note that this version of dsm is _not_ compatible with the Windows
program DISTANCE and can only be used in R. It will however be
incorporated into the next major DISTANCE release.

Finally, please do report any bugs to me and I will attempt to fix them
as quickly as possible.


--dave
